summary: Decoded two static class-data tables from wpcmk.ovr's file image: (1) class attribute-requirement table at file 0x5e98 (14 × 9 bytes, ASCII-encoded minimums like the race base table — byte - 0x41 = min stat), and (2) class skill-availability bitmaps at file 0x5cb8..0x5e93 (14 × 4 null-terminated digit strings of lengths [10,7,5,8] = 30 bits per class, matching the 30-byte skill block in the character record at +0x134..+0x151).
method: Direct file-byte read of wpcmk.ovr at the offsets identified by the prior wpcmk asm trace. The data is STATIC in the overlay file image (unlike the race base-stat table at DGROUP+0x52D9, which is loaded transiently at game_state=0x10).

findings.claim: Class attribute requirements at wpcmk file 0x5e98 use the same 'byte - 0x41' ASCII encoding as race base stats. 14 classes × 9 bytes (8 attribute minimums + 1 null). KAR slot is always 0 — Karma never gates class eligibility.

Skill-availability data at wpcmk file 0x5cb8..0x5e93 is 56 null-terminated ASCII '0'/'1' strings grouped 4-per-class. String lengths are consistent: [10, 7, 5, 8] = 30 bits total per class, matching the 30-slot skill block in the character record at +0x134..+0x151.

Decoded skill-availability bitmaps for all 14 classes. Per-class count of available skills: Fighter 13, Mage 11, Priest 10, Thief 17, Ranger 17, Alchemist 9, Bard 19, Psionic 11, Valkyrie 15, Bishop 11, Lord 15, Samurai 16, Monk 15, Ninja 19. Cross-validated against stock-character skill values (THESUS slot[1]=10, LYSANDR slot[15]=10, NOBAL slot[26]=7, TREON slot[28]=10 all correspond to '1' bits in their classes).

Slot-to-name mapping for the 30 skill slots is speculative (from martydill/Wizardry-6-reverse-engineering's SKILL_INDEX_MAP), cross-validated against stock-character values but not yet binary-verified against wpcmk asm. Slots 10, 17-21 are listed as 'holes' in martydill's map but the bitmaps occasionally set bits there for specific classes — the actual meaning of those slots needs further RE.

implications: Engine-faithful character creation can now use CLASS_REQUIREMENTS + RACE_BASE_STATS to compute exact eligibility: given (race, rolled attributes + bonus allocation), which of the 14 classes is the character eligible for? Direct lookup from the typed constants.

The 'absolute dogshit gaming experience' framing of the bonus-point lottery now has concrete numbers attached: e.g., to qualify for Bishop you need INT>=15 AND PIE>=15. Combined with the bonus-roll distribution (5+rng(6) + two 1-in-20 +8 chances, max=21) and race base stats, the per-roll qualification probability for each class is calculable.
Skill-availability bitmaps let the create flow filter the skill-allocation menu to only show training-eligible skills for the chosen class — engine-faithful behavior.

The slot-to-name mapping should be verified via wpcmk asm tracing in a follow-up: find the skill-display routine in wpcmk that iterates the bitmap and renders skill names, identify which engine string table holds the names.
